inputs.share_count_basis: 985,856,695 ordinary shares, unchanged since 2017; FY2025 AR note (line 13768) states the Group has no equity instruments that could dilute EPS, so basic = fully diluted. Held flat: LTIP awards are cash-settled (notional shares), so there is no SBC to expense and no grant dilution.
inputs.net_debt_basis: ATTRIBUTABLE net debt at 30 June 2026 as disclosed by the company (H1 2026 report p.22): attributable borrowings $6,090.7m less attributable cash and liquid investments $3,378.9m = $2,711.8m. Consolidated figures are borrowings $8,126.2m, cash+liquid investments $4,160.1m, net debt $3,966.1m; the $1,254m difference is the partners' share of Los Pelambres / Centinela / Antucoya project debt and cash. Used because the flows are attributable-only (see cash_tax_rate_note) -- charging 65% of the flows against 100% of the debt would charge the minorities twice.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR accounting policy (Q) Share-based payments: all long-term incentive awards are CASH-settled and linked to a notional number of shares; no equity-settled share-based payment charge exists in the cash flow statement. SBC-zero market treatment: SBC rows kept explicit at 0%, house = street, band_position null.
inputs.fx_note: Statements, flows and WACC are USD; the LSE quote is GBp (pence, 1/100 GBP). fx_rate = GBp per USD = 100 / GBPUSD 1.3240 (Yahoo GBPUSD=X, 2026-10-02T21:29:47Z) = 75.53. All per-share values are computed in USD and multiplied by 75.53 to reach the quote currency; the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv are in GBp so they compare directly to current_price. Parity check: no liquid dual listing exists (the OTC ADR ANFGY is 1:1 but too thin to use), so the direction is verified by magnitude instead -- a USD value of ~$19/share must print as ~1,400p, not 0.25p or 14p.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-02T15:36:13Z (regular LSE close, Friday 2 October 2026; fetched Monday 5 October before the session's first print -- replace with the 5 October close when available; not an after-hours print)
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate: 10y UST ~4.2% + beta ~1.15 x ERP 5% = cost of equity ~10%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.6% (Sep-2025 plc bond coupon 5.625%, Fitch BBB+) = ~3.6% after 36% tax; attributable debt ~15% of capital -> WACC ~9.0%. Same 9.0% in all three scenarios: copper-price cyclicality, Chile concentration and tax-reform risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked again in the discount rate (risk charged once).
inputs.lease_treatment: (A) Leases as debt. IFRS 16 lease liabilities ($162m consolidated at FY2025; larger after the Centinela SIAM II water-infrastructure lease recognised in H1 2026) sit inside the borrowings figure the company nets into attributable net debt, so lease principal is NOT deducted from the flows. The leases are equipment embedded in mining service contracts; their renewal is implicitly inside the sustaining-capex % path. Lease interest is a financing cost and is outside the unlevered flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: Attributable-only flows: the NCI profit share (Los Pelambres 40%, Centinela 30%, Antucoya 30% held by Marubeni, JX and Mitsubishi; FY2023-FY2025 share of profit after tax 35.7% / 37.0% / 35.8%, H1 2026 33.7%) is folded into the cash_tax_rate driver as a combined leakage rate, and the net-debt bridge uses the company's attributable figure. No separate NCI deduction is made. Calibration: FY2025 EBIT $3,506.5m x (1 - 0.584) = $1,459m vs reported attributable net income $1,328.9m + after-tax attributable net interest (~$132m) = $1,461m -- ties. The one residual is that the engine adds back 100% of D&A and deducts 100% of capex while the partners fund ~35% of the FY2026-27 capex-over-D&A gap; that is restored as a computed equity-bridge item.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Owner-FCF DCF, component route, with the cyclical/non-US adaptations (currency bridge, leases-as-debt, NCI folded into leakage, SBC-zero, risk charged once). Chosen because Antofagasta is an operating copper miner whose value is a stream of free cash flow; it is not a bank/REIT/LIC and there is no live corporate action. First valuation of this ticker (no MEMORY entry). THROUGH-CYCLE: FY2025 ($8.6bn revenue, 60.3% margin) and H1 2026 (63.4%) are peak-cycle prints -- copper and gold at records -- so the forward path reverts realised prices toward a ~$4.50/lb nominal mid-cycle copper price over FY2027-29 while volume rises ~30% as the Centinela Second Concentrator and Los Pelambres Growth Enabling Projects commission in 2027; the terminal EBITDA margin of 55% sits above the FY2017-24 average (~52%) to reflect the structurally lower-cost expanded Centinela and by-product credits, and well below FY2025/H1-26. FLOWS BASIS: group EBITDA including the share of associates/JVs (Zaldivar 50%, Buenaventura 18.94%; ~$183m of FY2025's $5,201.9m) is kept in the margin, so no associate value is added in the bridge (matching-asset rule). INTEREST INCOME: $156.2m FY2025 is NOT stripped -- the company is net-debt, and the forward flows are built from EBITDA so interest never enters them; attributable cash is netted in the bridge. REPORTED FCF: OCF $3,071.6m - capex $3,684.5m = -$612.9m in FY2025 is a capex-peak artefact (growth capex ~$2.3bn), not a run-rate; last_fcf equals reported_fcf because SBC is nil and interest is not stripped. CASH TAX DRIVER: cash_tax_rate_path is a COMBINED leakage (income tax + royalty + NCI share), not the statutory rate -- see assumptions.base.cash_tax_rate_note. TERMINAL: cap 15x attributable FCF (~5.7x attributable EBITDA at a 55% margin) is the cyclical cap; it binds in base and bull, Gordon binds in bear. The market multiple today (~9x consolidated EV/EBITDA on peak FY2026E earnings, ~25x P/E) is a premium Antofagasta has carried for a decade (Luksic control, 50-year reserve life, scarce free float); the gap between this model and the price is the cost of (a) copper staying above $5/lb rather than reverting and (b) that premium multiple persisting.

equity_bridge.item: NCI partners' 35% share of FY2026-30 capex in excess of D&A (restores attributable FCF; the leakage driver applies at EBIT only)
equity_bridge.note: Base path: capex - D&A = +$1,835m FY2026, +$1,019m FY2027, +$114m FY2028, -$118m FY2029, -$60m FY2030, ~0 thereafter (capex = D&A at 20% of revenue). The engine deducts 100% of that gap from attributable NOPAT, but Marubeni/JX/Mitsubishi fund ~35% of it at Los Pelambres, Centinela and Antucoya. 0.35 x gap, discounted at 9%: 589 + 301 + 31 - 29 - 14 = $878m -> $880m. Bear/bull equivalents are ~$800m / ~$950m; the base figure is used for all three (spread < $0.1/share).

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 6.0% vs revenue 10.9% and EPS 21.3% (>30% divergence). The revenue/EPS CAGRs run from the FY2020 copper trough ($2.80/lb) to the FY2025 record ($4.5+/lb, gold at records) and overstate underlying growth; the equity CAGR is held down by a 35-50% dividend payout. None of the CAGRs drives the projection -- the forward path is volume (+30% by FY2028-29 from Centinela/Pelambres) x a mid-cycle price reversion; 6.0% is recorded only as the downstream PEG proxy.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series equals reported FCF (SBC nil, interest not stripped). FCF CAGRs are undefined: FY2020 $752.8m -> FY2025 -$612.9m and FY2022 -$2.3m -> FY2025 -$612.9m, because FY2022-25 is the growth-capex supercycle (capex $1.9bn -> $3.7bn). Pre-supercycle FCF: FY2017 $1,196m, FY2019 $1,017m, FY2021 $1,897m (all consolidated, pre-NCI dividends of $120-605m). EPS 3yr CAGR is negative because FY2022 EPS included the $944.7m gain on the Reko Diq/JV disposal.

base.growth_rates_note: FY2026 +17% to ~$10.1bn: H1 $4,479m on 267.8kt sold ($16.7k per copper tonne incl. by-products); guidance 625-655kt implies ~355kt H2 sales at similar realised prices (~$5.9bn H2 at run-rate; +17% leaves ~$0.3bn headroom). FY2027 +1%: volume +9% (~700kt) offset by copper reverting ~7% toward mid-cycle and gold/moly off their peaks. FY2028 +12%: volume +17% (~820kt) as the Second Concentrator reaches full rate, price -4%. FY2029 +3%: ~850kt, price settles ~$4.50/lb nominal. FY2030+ 2.5%: volumes flat (grade decline offset by Zaldivar 2051 extension), price with inflation. Terminal FY2035 revenue ~$13.6bn = ~$5.8/lb copper-equivalent per tonne sold in 2026 dollars vs $7.6 today -- a ~20% real reversion.
base.ebitda_margin_note: Group EBITDA incl. associates. FY2026 62% (H1 63.4%, H2 carries the Los Pelambres weather shutdown and higher cash costs before by-products at $2.85/lb). Reverts with price to 55% mid-cycle: FY2017-24 average ~52%, FY2021 (copper $4.23) 64.7%, FY2022-24 ($3.8-4.1) 49-52%; 55% credits the expanded, lower-cost Centinela and structurally higher by-product credits, and sits well below FY2025's 60.3%.
base.da_pct_note: FY2025 D&A $1,695m = 19.7% of revenue; H1 2026 $733.5m annualises to ~$1.5bn (15% on a bigger revenue base). Rises to ~$1.9bn FY2027 and ~$2.3bn FY2028 as the $4.4bn Second Concentrator and Pelambres projects enter depreciation, then 20% of revenue, equal to terminal capex.
base.capex_pct_note: FY2026 = $3.4bn guidance (held after the shutdown). FY2027 ~$2.9bn (Centinela completion, Zaldivar $0.9bn pipeline over 2026-28, Pelambres desal/pipeline). FY2028 ~$2.4bn, FY2029 ~$2.2bn. FY2031+ 20% of revenue (= D&A): ~$1.3-1.5bn sustaining + ~$0.4bn mine development + life-extension spend for an ~850kt producer, in nominal dollars. Management: 'past peak capital expenditure for the current growth phase'.
base.cash_tax_rate_note: COMBINED LEAKAGE, not a statutory rate: income tax + Chilean mining royalty + withholding at a 36% effective rate (FY2025 underlying ETR 36.2%, FY2024 38.1%), then the ~35% NCI share of post-tax profit: 0.36 + 0.64 x 0.35 = 58.4%. Applied to EBIT it yields attributable NOPAT (FY2025 calibration ties within $2m -- see inputs.nci_treatment). Cash taxes paid lag the charge ($708m paid vs $1,088m charged in FY2025; $927m paid in H1 2026 as the catch-up arrived), so the accrual rate is the right long-run cash rate. Chile's pending reform (corporate 27% -> 23% with stability agreements vs a higher royalty) is assumed net-neutral in base.
base.wc_capture_note: Receivables (provisionally priced concentrate) and inventories exceed payables; growth consumes ~5% of the revenue increase. Negative, per the manufacturer/distributor rule.

bull.growth_rates_note: Structural-deficit case: copper holds above $5/lb through FY2028 and gold stays near record; H2 2026 sales catch up fully (FY2026 ~$10.4bn); both projects commission on schedule and ramp to +30% by FY2029 with Zaldivar's primary-sulphide leach adding volume from FY2030.
bull.ebitda_margin_note: Margins stay near the FY2025/H1-26 level while the Second Concentrator lowers unit costs; drift to 58% terminal (slightly above FY2025) as grades decline.
bull.capex_pct_note: Same dollar programme on a larger revenue base; sustaining settles at 19% of revenue with capex marginally below D&A as the growth assets depreciate.
bull.cash_tax_rate_note: Combined leakage with a 34% tax rate (corporate cut to 23% partly offsets royalty) and 35% NCI: 0.34 + 0.66 x 0.35 = 57.1%.

bear.growth_rates_note: Cyclical-downturn case: H2 2026 recovery from the Pelambres shutdown is incomplete (FY2026 ~$9.7bn); FY2027 copper falls to ~$3.75/lb on a China slowdown and the supply response to 2026 prices, gold and molybdenum retrace; the Second Concentrator slips a year on the flotation-area geotechnical issues (volume +6% FY2028, flat FY2029); long-run 2% as grade decline is only partly offset.
bear.ebitda_margin_note: FY2027-29 at 47-50%, the FY2018-19/FY2022-23 trough band ($2.7-3.9/lb copper), with higher water and cost-inflation drag; 48% terminal.
bear.capex_pct_note: Committed growth capex cannot be cut in FY2026-27 (same dollars on lower revenue), and water/sustaining spend stays at 21% of revenue thereafter (= D&A).
bear.cash_tax_rate_note: Combined leakage with a 40% tax rate (royalty reform lands unfavourably, management's 48-50% total-burden warning partly realised) and 35% NCI: 0.40 + 0.60 x 0.35 = 61.0%.

scenario_narratives.base: Copper reverts from the 2026 record toward a ~$4.50/lb nominal mid-cycle over FY2027-29 just as the Centinela Second Concentrator and Los Pelambres Growth Enabling Projects lift volume ~30% to ~850kt by FY2029, so group revenue climbs only modestly from the FY2026 peak and the EBITDA margin settles at 55% -- above the FY2017-24 average because the expanded Centinela is lower-cost and by-product credits are structurally larger, below FY2025/H1-26. Capex falls from $3.4bn to roughly D&A by FY2031, turning the FY2025-26 negative FCF into ~$1.8-2.0bn a year of attributable FCF. Chile's tax/royalty reform is net-neutral; the ~35% minority leakage persists. The axes are the copper price path, project timing, and the Chilean fiscal regime.
scenario_narratives.bull: The structural copper deficit (electrification, grid, AI data centres; JPM's ~330kt 2026 shortfall) keeps copper above $5/lb through the decade's end and gold near records, so margins hold ~60% while volume rises 30% on schedule and Zaldivar's primary-sulphide leach adds a further leg from FY2030. Twin Metals and Cachorro/Encierro add long-dated optionality not in the numbers. Even here the terminal multiple is the 15x cyclical cap, not the market's current premium.
scenario_narratives.bear: A China slowdown and the supply response to 2026 prices take copper to ~$3.75/lb in FY2027 while gold and molybdenum retrace; the Second Concentrator slips a year on the flotation-area geotechnical issues; the Chilean royalty package lands unfavourably (tax leakage 40%); committed capex cannot be cut, so FY2026-28 attributable FCF is near zero and the margin spends three years in the 47-50% trough band before a 48% terminal. Single-country concentration (the July 2026 Coquimbo shutdown) is the recurring reminder that all four mines share one regulator and one climate.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised from 15% to 25%: a commodity price distribution around mid-cycle is roughly symmetric, the stock sits at the top of a record-price cycle, and the pending Chilean royalty/tax reform plus 100% single-country concentration are live, correlated downside risks. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to hold at once -- copper sustained above $5/lb, both projects commissioning on time, and a benign fiscal outcome -- and the market price already assumes most of that.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Through-cycle owner-FCF valuation of a top-5 pure-play copper miner at a cyclical peak. The model does not extrapolate FY2025/H1-26 record margins; it reverts realised prices to a mid-cycle level while crediting the +30% volume step-up and the post-peak capex decline, charges the ~35% minority leakage and attributable net debt exactly once, discounts USD flows at a USD WACC with no scenario-specific risk premium, and caps the terminal at 15x attributable FCF. The resulting value sits far below the market price: the difference is the price of copper staying above $5/lb in perpetuity plus the premium multiple (~25x P/E, ~9x EV/EBITDA on peak earnings) Antofagasta has carried for a decade on Luksic control, 50-year reserve life and scarce free float. A 15% hurdle entry price is correspondingly well below the IV.
key_risks_to_valuation: Mid-cycle copper price assumption (~$4.50/lb nominal): every $0.50/lb is roughly 8-9pp of EBITDA margin at ~850kt, worth ~$0.5bn of attributable FCF a year
Chilean tax and royalty reform could move the combined leakage several points either way (base 58.4%, bear 61%, bull 57%)
Centinela Second Concentrator and Los Pelambres project timing and cost: a one-year slip removes most of the FY2028 revenue step and defers the capex decline
Terminal multiple: the 15x cyclical cap vs the market's premium; lifting the cap to the market multiple roughly doubles the value and is the whole gap to the price
NCI leakage assumed at 35% of post-tax profit; Centinela growth (30% NCI) lowers it slightly, a Los Pelambres-heavy mix raises it
Single-country climate/regulatory events (July 2026 Coquimbo 'state of catastrophe' shutdown) and water-scarcity capex that peers in water-rich jurisdictions do not carry
FX: value is built in USD and converted at GBPUSD 1.324; a 5% move in sterling moves the pence IV 5% with no change in the business
